attribution.note: Co-authored Marcus on AI post (Marcus and Davis). The sentence is the authors' own assertion, so Marcus endorses it.

semantics.note: Reading 'reasonable abilities' as reasoning abilities is a fair correction of an apparent typo. 'Reliably', the word-problem scope and both GPT-4 and the plug-ins are all kept.

contract.note: Plain reading (recurring failures to formulate the math correctly, not a total lack of knowledge) is ordinary and fair. 'Reliably' has no threshold, so the result depends on interpretation, as the contract flags.

evidence.note: Pre-post 2023 preprint (Sept 16). One Code Interpreter trace shows a spatial formulation error on an advanced physics problem, corrected when the model was questioned. A single example on non-ordinary problems, with no Wolfram Alpha data, cannot show recurring failures across configurations. Labelled counterevidence, but it does not contradict the claim.

reviews.rationale: The support condition needs independent traces showing recurring commonsense formulation errors across GPT-4 and both plug-in setups. The packet has one anecdotal Code Interpreter failure on an advanced physics problem, and nothing on Wolfram Alpha or ordinary word problems. Nothing shows dependable translation either. The evidence settles neither side.

attribution.note: Opening sentence of the co-authored post, written and endorsed by the authors.

semantics.note: Dropping 'notoriously' slightly narrows the wording but keeps the core claim of struggling with calculations. Scope (GPT-4 and similar current LLMs) is kept.

contract.note: Plain reading (frequent calculation errors without tools, not failure on every calculation) is the ordinary meaning of 'struggle'. Excluding specialised arithmetic models fits the speaker's focus on general-purpose systems.

evidence.note: Sept 2023 primary evaluation, before the post. GPT-4 gets 18.84% and ChatGPT 10% exact accuracy on 9,592 arithmetic cases, which are substantial error rates.

Specialised MathGLM reaches high accuracy. That bears on whether LLM architecture can calculate well, not on whether general-purpose GPT-4-class models struggled. The same source gives GPT-4 4.3% on multi-digit multiplication.

reviews.rationale: A primary evaluation from before the post shows GPT-4 and ChatGPT with low exact-answer accuracy on unaided arithmetic. This meets the support condition of substantial calculation error rates. The specialised-model result is a qualification outside the general-purpose scope and does not contradict the claim.

attribution.note: Authors' own conclusion in the co-authored post.

semantics.note: Keeps 'in all the ways' and 'perfectly capable', so the claim denies full human-level competence, not all competence. The part about what humans imagine is framing only.

contract.note: Plain reading (a material gap compared with instructed humans on tasks humans can manage) fits the universal wording being denied. It does not assume humans are perfect.

evidence.note: Independent May 2023 preprint. GPT-4 produces executable Blocksworld plans only about 34% of the time in a simple common-sense domain that humans find easy. The human baseline (39/50) is cited from the same section but is not shown in the excerpt.

reviews.rationale: The claim only denies that LLMs match humans in every way. A reproducible gap on a simple planning task that instructed humans largely solve meets the support condition. Nothing in the packet shows human-general competence across the claimed scope.
